nonLabourLines.description: Stripe/payment provider fees and sandbox setup
Contingency for third-party/legacy system integration risk

assumptions: The rate card provided is a PLACEHOLDER: all project members are currently a single undifferentiated 'Team member' role at $75/hr with only 1 FTE available. These costs are indicative only and MUST be re-estimated once real roles (e.g. developer, QA, designer, PM) and their hourly rates are assigned.

With only 1 FTE available and 24 backlog items totalling 178 story points, the role is staffed far too thinly to deliver this backlog in a normal timeframe; 1,520 hours at 1 FTE implies roughly 9-10 months of continuous full-time work with zero allowance for illness, leave, meetings, or parallel workstreams (e.g. QA, design, PM happening concurrently). This is flagged as a major staffing risk, not just a cost one.

No historical actuals (real spend/velocity data) exist for this project yet, so hours per story point are estimated using an industry-typical heuristic (~8.5 hours/point average, adjusted per task complexity) rather than derived from past performance. This should be revisited once real velocity data is available.

Story points were converted to hours using an approximate blended rate of 8-9 hours per point, with adjustments upward for high-complexity/high-risk items (legacy data migration, payment integration, multi-currency) and downward for well-scoped smaller items.

Non-labour costs are rough placeholders for third-party tooling/fees (Stripe integration, Oracle migration tooling, CI/hosting infrastructure) and a general contingency for integration risk; actual figures depend on vendor contracts not yet in place.

Scenario range (Optimistic/Most Likely/Pessimistic) reflects general uncertainty in a single-resource, placeholder-rate estimate rather than statistically derived percentiles, since no historical throughput data exists.

PW-8 (Legacy data migration, 21 points) and PW-7 (Payment provider integration, 13 points) are treated as the highest-risk, highest-effort items given data volume and financial/compliance sensitivity, and are weighted with extra hours accordingly.
Priority breakdown totals are apportioned from the labour cost based on each task's estimated hours within its priority band, plus a pro-rata share of non-labour costs.
input.reasoning: Backlog totals 178 story points across 24 tasks. Using a blended estimate of ~8-9 hours per point (with extra weighting for high-risk items like legacy migration and payment integration, and slightly less for well-understood UI/CRUD tasks), total effort was estimated at ~1,520 hours. At the placeholder rate of $75/hr for the single 'Team member' role, this gives a labour cost of $114,000. Non-labour costs of $6,000 were added for third-party tooling (Stripe, Oracle migration tooling), CI/staging infrastructure, and integration risk contingency, bringing the Most Likely total to $120,000. Optimistic (-15%) and Pessimistic (+25%) scenarios reflect the wide uncertainty inherent in: (a) a placeholder single-role rate card, (b) only 1 FTE tasked with a backlog that would typically require a small multi-role team, and (c) no historical velocity data to calibrate estimates. Priority breakdown apportions the labour cost across Urgent/High/Medium/Low backlog items based on their estimated hours, with a pro-rata share of non-labour costs added to each band.

reductions.description: Descope PW-18 (Admin back-office for support staff, Low priority, 13 points) from this phase; support agents can continue using existing tools until a later release.
reductions.effect: Removes an entire Low-priority feature from initial delivery, deferring ~110 hours of effort.

reductions.description: Defer PW-19 (Usage analytics and reporting, Low priority, 8 points) and PW-23 (Contract tests against helpdesk API, Low priority, 5 points) to a post-launch phase.
reductions.effect: Removes two Low-priority, non-customer-blocking items (~100 hours combined), reducing scope without affecting core launch functionality.

reductions.description: Reduce PW-14 (Multi-currency support, Medium priority, 13 points) to a single-currency launch (USD only) and defer EUR/PLN support.
reductions.effect: Cuts FX-rate integration, settlement and display complexity by roughly 60%, saving ~80 hours; multi-currency can be added once portal is live and demand is confirmed.

reductions.description: Staff the project with at least 2-3 differentiated FTEs (developer, QA, designer) instead of the current 1 FTE placeholder, and negotiate a real rate card before committing to the Most Likely total.
reductions.effect: Does not reduce cost directly, but is essential to make the schedule feasible; attempting to force the full backlog through 1 FTE at $75/hr will blow out timeline even if dollar total stays similar, effectively increasing real-world cost through delay.

reductions.description: Delay non-labour spend on CI/staging infrastructure and Oracle migration tooling until PW-1 and PW-8 are actually scheduled to start, rather than provisioning upfront.
reductions.effect: Shifts ~$1,500 of infrastructure and tooling spend later in the timeline, improving near-term cash flow without changing total scope.
